body.x: Hurotics (CEO Giuk Lee), a wearable robotics specialist, has been honored with two CES 2025 Innovation Awards in the Accessibility & AgeTech and Robotics categories for its hospital-use wearable rehabilitation robot H-Medi. This marks the company’s second consecutive year receiving CES Innovation Awards.

The Consumer Technology Association (CTA) organizes CES 2025, the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition, which will take place in Las Vegas in January. The CTA grants CES Innovation Awards to products that showcase groundbreaking technologies that lead the industry.

H-Medi, developed with support from the Pan-Ministry Medical Device Development Program in collaboration with Chung-Ang University Hospital, Chung-Ang University, and RoboWell Korea, is a wearable rehabilitation robot designed for hospital use. The device employs AI to analyze the wearer’s gait and delivers personalized rehabilitation therapy. Lightweight and comfortable, it can be worn like everyday clothing or carried in a bag, enabling effective treatment beyond the confines of a rehabilitation clinic.

According to Hurotics, “H-Medi, recognized this year, and H-Flex, awarded last year, are flagship products in our wellness lineup. These innovations address the global challenge of population aging, earning us this prestigious recognition.”

Giuk Lee, CEO of Hurotics, stated, “Receiving Innovation Awards for two consecutive years at CES demonstrates our technological prowess and commitment to innovation. As a leader in practical and accessible wearable robotics, we are dedicated to developing robots that can make a meaningful difference for patients worldwide.”
